description: Alcohol pharmacokinetics (Widmark model, zero-order elimination) and well-established hepatic biomarkers. Organ/system level by default; biomarkers only where clinically validated (brief 1.5).

standard_drink_grams.citation: NIAAA, Rethinking Drinking (US standard drink = 14 g pure ethanol)
standard_drink_grams.notes: US definition. UK unit = 8 g, EU often 10 g. Convert at input boundary.

widmark_r_male.citation: Watson 1981; Posey & Mozayani 2007 (mean r male ~0.68-0.71, SD ~0.085)
widmark_r_male.notes: Fraction of body mass that distributes ethanol. Higher = more body water.

widmark_r_female.citation: Watson 1981; Posey & Mozayani 2007 (mean r female ~0.55, SD ~0.055)
widmark_r_female.notes: Lower than male due to lower average body-water fraction.

elimination_rate_beta.unit: g/100mL per hour (BAC decline per hour)
elimination_rate_beta.citation: Jones 2010, 'Evidence-based survey of the elimination rates of ethanol' (mean ~0.015-0.018, range 0.010-0.025)
elimination_rate_beta.notes: Zero-order kinetics: BAC declines linearly once absorption complete. Higher in habitual drinkers.

absorption_rate_ka.citation: Norberg et al. 2003 (absorption half-life ~5-10 min fasting; t_peak ~30-45 min)
absorption_rate_ka.notes: Used to model the rising limb. Food in stomach slows this substantially (lower ka).

blood_water_factor.citation: Widmark formula standard constant (BAC in g/100mL)
blood_water_factor.notes: Embedded in the classic Widmark form; kept explicit for traceability.

ALT.notes: Hepatocellular injury marker. Future output of hepatic module under chronic load; NOT modeled in v1 (no validated short-horizon dose-response from BAC alone).

AST.notes: AST:ALT ratio > 2 suggestive of alcoholic liver injury. Future biomarker output; not modeled in v1.
